missing.item: Evidence that early market closure is intended to let lenders withdraw despite an unexpired fixed term.
missing.why: The code supports the withdrawal revert after closure, but the impact depends on whether the fixed-term restriction should end when the market closes. The record identifies no policy or documentation establishing that expectation.
missing.resolves_when: Provide a cited policy clause or documentation establishing that closing a market must permit lender withdrawals before the fixed-term end time.

missing.item: Evidence clarifying the practical severity of the time-limited withdrawal delay.
missing.why: The record says the restriction ends when the fixed term expires, so the demonstrated effect is a delay rather than permanent loss. This limits support for a higher severity.
missing.resolves_when: Document the maximum remaining lock duration and any concrete consequences of that delay relevant to severity.

reason: The passes disagreed (NEEDS_PROOF). Route this report to a human reviewer.

evidence.claim: FixedTermLoanHooks.onQueueWithdrawal blocks all withdrawals until fixedTermEndTime, and closing the market does not reset fixedTermEndTime, so lenders cannot exit even after the borrower closes the market.
evidence.support_reason: onQueueWithdrawal reverts with WithdrawBeforeTermEnd whenever fixedTermEndTime > block.timestamp (L857-859), unconditionally and before any closed-market consideration. onCloseMarket is a no-op (L943-946) and the constructor config does not set Bit_Enabled_CloseMarket (L154-157), so fixedTermEndTime is never cleared on close. closeMarket (WildcatMarket.sol L226-287) does not touch the hook. Thus a closed market with an unexpired fixed term still reverts on queueWithdrawal/queueFullWithdrawal.
preconditions: Market deployed with FixedTermLoanHooks and fixedTermEndTime in the future

missing_evidence.item: Whether the fixed-term lock is intended to survive market closure (design intent), i.e. whether 'lenders can always exit a closed market' is a protocol invariant the borrower closing early violates.
missing_evidence.why: The impact 'lenders cannot exit' depends on treating the fixed-term lock as invalid after close. The docs describe fixed-term as a deliberate withdrawal restriction; if the lock is intended to persist through closure, the demonstrated revert is expected behavior, not a vulnerability. No cited policy clause establishes that closure must override the fixed term.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A cited policy clause or docs statement establishes that closing a market must allow lenders to withdraw regardless of fixed-term end time.

missing_evidence.item: Whether the borrower can simply wait out the term or whether funds are permanently stuck (temporary vs permanent lock).
missing_evidence.why: The lock is time-bounded (max 365 days); lenders can withdraw after fixedTermEndTime passes, so the effect is a delay, not permanent loss. This affects severity but not whether the path is reachable.
